extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students in mathematical logic and computability theory
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook chapter explaining Gödel-numbering (coding) of symbols/terms/formulas/derivations, primitive-recursive tests and functions on these codes, and representability of computable functions in Robinson's Q, including simulation of primitive recursion via the beta function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decidability from completeness for axiomatizable consistent theories
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ is consistent, axiomatizable, and complete then Γ is decidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate all theorems of Γ by dovetailing derivations; because Γ is complete, either α or ¬α will appear and the procedure decides membership. Used in the corollary arguing Q must be incomplete when it represents all decidable properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: incompleteness from representing all decidable properties
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ is consistent, axiomatizable, and represents every decidable property, then Γ is not complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Γ were complete, by the previous criterion it would be decidable. But representing every decidable property implies Γ is not decidable, contradiction; thus Γ is incomplete. The proof guarantees existence of independent sentences but not an explicit example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: Presburger arithmetic is complete and decidable
rubrics_metrics.description: Pres = {α ∈ LA+ : |=B α}, the theory of arithmetic without multiplication, is both complete and decidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates that not every sufficiently interesting theory meets Gödel's hypotheses; absence of × makes Presburger arithmetic decidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol coding scheme (Definition 161A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a unique code cs to each symbol s of the language L: logical symbols get fixed pair codes ⟨0,k⟩; the i-th variable vi gets ⟨1,i⟩; the i-th constant ci gets ⟨2,i⟩; the i-th n-ary function symbol f^n_i gets ⟨3,n,i⟩; the i-th n-ary predicate P^n_i gets ⟨4,n,i⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a computable bijection so symbol → code is computable and information like arity can be recovered. Example table for logical symbols is given (⊥ → ⟨0,0⟩, ¬ → ⟨0,1⟩, …).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fn(x,n) and Pred(x,n) are primitive recursive (Proposition 161B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation Fn(x,n) (x is code of some n-ary function symbol) and Pred(x,n) (x is code of some n-ary predicate symbol or equality when n = 2) are primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because symbol codes carry arity and category information, these relations are computable by primitive recursive tests on the code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Godel number of a sequence (Definition 161C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If s0,...,sn−1 is a sequence of symbols, its Gödel number is ⟨cs0, ..., csn−1⟩ (the chosen sequence-coding, e.g., power-of-primes). Distinguish symbol codes cs from Gödel numbers #s# which code sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: variable v5 has symbol code ⟨1,5⟩ while the term v5 as a sequence has Gödel number ⟨⟨1,5⟩⟩; power-of-primes coding formula provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term(x) and ClTerm(x) are primitive recursive (Proposition 162A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation Term(x) (x is the Gödel number of a term) and ClTerm(x) (x is the Gödel number of a closed term) are primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express existence of a formation sequence y coding how the term is built from variables, constants, and n-ary function symbols using bounded quantification; show there is a primitive-recursive bound on y (e.g., ≤ p^{k}(x+1) where k = len(x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: num(n) = #n# is primitive recursive (Proposition 162B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The function num(n) that returns the Gödel number of the numeral for n is primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined by primitive recursion: num(0)=#0#, num(n+1)=#′(# ⌢ num(n) ⌢ #)#.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic-wff recognition Atom(x) is primitive recursive (Proposition 163A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Atom(x) holds iff x is the Gödel number of an atomic formula: either a predicate P^n_j applied to n terms or equality =(t1,t2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test existence of appropriate n, j and a sequence z of term Gödel numbers with bounded quantifiers; use Term(z_i) and concatenation tests, all primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formed formula Frm(x) is primitive recursive (Proposition 163B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frm(x) holds iff x is the Gödel number of a well-formed formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a formation sequence s0,...,sk−1 of wffs whose codes are all < x; express the inductive formation condition with bounded quantification to get primitive recursiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free occurrence relation FreeOcc(x,z,i) is primitive recursive (Proposition 163C)
rubrics_metrics.description: FreeOcc(x, z, i) holds iff the i-th symbol of the formula with Gödel number x is a free occurrence of the variable with code z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked as an exercise in text; follows from substring/subterm tests and Frm/Var/Term relations being primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sent(x) (x is a sentence) is primitive recursive (Proposition 163D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sent(x) holds iff x is the Gödel number of a sentence (a wff with no free occurrences of variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express as bounded quantification: for all i < len(x) and for all z < x, if z is a variable code then ¬FreeOcc(x,z,i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution function Subst(x,y,z) is primitive recursive (Proposition 164A)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a primitive recursive function Subst such that Subst(#α#, #t#, #u#) = #α[t/u]#.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define hSubst by primitive recursion over positions: at each position append y if FreeOcc(x,z,i) holds, otherwise append the original symbol. Then Subst(x,y,z) = hSubst(x,y,z,len(x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeFor(x,y,z) is primitive recursive (Proposition 164B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation FreeFor(x,y,z) (term with Gödel number y is free for variable z in formula x) is primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked as exercise; follows from Subst and FreeOcc primitive-recursive tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation coding (Definition 165A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If δ is an axiomatic derivation consisting of wffs α1,...,αn then #δ# is ⟨#α1#, ..., #αn#⟩ (the Gödel number of the sequence of codes of its lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This representation lets one compute last-line, individual lines, etc., by primitive-recursive operations on sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive-recursive tests for derivation correctness (Proposition 165C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following relations about derivations are primitive recursive: (1) IsAx(n): n is an instance of an axiom schema; (2) MP(d,i): i-th line in d is justified by modus ponens; (3) QR1/QR2(d,i): i-th line justified by quantified-rule (qr); (4) Deriv(d): d is a correct derivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IsAx test occurrence of appropriate sub-wffs b,c with concatenation equations; MP(d,i) expressed by bounded search for j,k<i with matching α and α→β patterns; QR expressed by tests for β→∀x α(x) together with a previous β→α[c/x] line and side-conditions (const c not in β); Deriv(d) is universal closure over lines: each line is axiom or MP or QR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prf_Γ(x,y) primitive recursive when Γ is primitive recursive (Proposition 165D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ is a primitive recursive set of sentences then Prf_Γ(x,y) (x is code of a derivation of the sentence with Gödel number y from Γ) is primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Deriv(x) for correctness of derivation and the deduction theorem: test that last line of x is Cond(s,y) where s is a finite sequence of antecedents all in Γ, with bounded search for s; concatenation and membership tests are primitive recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of representability in Q (Definition 170A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function f(x0,...,xk) is representable in Q if there is a formula α_f(x0,...,xk,y) such that whenever f(n0,...,nk)=m, Q proves (1) α_f(n0,...,nk,m) and (2) ∀y (α_f(n0,...,nk,y) → m = y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently Q could prove ∀y (α_f(n0,...,nk,y) ↔ y = m). This requires Q to prove existence of the correct value and uniqueness in Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence: representability in Q iff computability (Theorem 170B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function is representable in Q if and only if it is computable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: left-to-right uses arithmetization of syntax and proof-search to show representable ⇒ recursive; right-to-left shows every general recursive function is representable in Q by showing basic functions are representable and representable functions closed under composition and regular minimization (and simulating primitive recursion via minimization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness lemma for representable functions (Lemma 171A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is representable in Q then there is α_f such that Q ⊢ α_f(n0,...,nk,m) iff m = f(n0,...,nk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representability conditions and consistency of Q: if Q proved α_f(n, m) with m ≠ f(n), contradiction arises from uniqueness condition and Q proving both equality and inequality in the standard model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representable functions are computable (Lemma 171B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every function representable in Q is computable (recursive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given α_f, enumerate derivations and search for a derivation of α_f(n,m); since Q proves α_f(n,f(n)) and Prf_Q is primitive recursive, define a regular relation R(n,s) that holds when s encodes a pair (derivation-code, m) proving α_f(n,m); f(n) = (µs R(n,s))_1. Formalize using Subst and Prf_Q and regular minimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese Remainder (Sunzi's) Theorem (Theorem 172D) as coding tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Given pairwise relatively prime moduli x0,...,xn and arbitrary remainders y0,...,yn there is z with z ≡ yi (mod xi) for each i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to encode finite sequences by picking moduli xi larger than yi; then z recovers yi as remainder of division by xi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta function lemma (Lemma 172A)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a function β(d,i) computable from basic functions (using composition and regular minimization, with add,mult,χ= allowed) such that for every finite sequence a0,...,an there is d with β(d,i)=ai for all i ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: pick j = max(n, a0+1,...), m = lcm(1,...,j), set xi = 1+(i+1)m which are pairwise coprime and > ai; by Chinese Remainder pick d0 with d0 ≡ ai (mod xi); set d = J(d0,d1) and define β(d,i)=rem(1+(i+1)d1, d0). β is definable using pairing J and remainder rem built from minimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation of primitive recursion via beta and minimization (Lemma 173A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If h is defined from f and g by primitive recursion (h(x,0)=f(x); h(x,y+1)=g(x,y,h(x,y))) then h can be defined from f,g and basic functions using only composition and regular minimization (no primitive recursion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ĥ(x,y) = least d coding sequence with β(d,0)=f(x) and for each i<y, β(d,i+1)=g(x,i,β(d,i)); then h(x,y)=β(ĥ(x,y),y). Use beta lemma to ensure regularity and express the minimization without primitive recursion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic arithmetic functions representable in Q (Section 17.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zero, successor, projections, characteristic equality χ=, addition and multiplication are representable in Q by natural formulas: α_zero(x,y) ≡ y = 0; α_succ(x,y) ≡ y = x′; α_P^n_i(...) ≡ y = x_i; α_χ=(x0,x1,y) ≡ (x0 = x1 ∧ y = 1) ∨ (x0 ≠ x1 ∧ y = 0); addition represented by (x0 + x1) = y, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs require showing Q proves the intended instances (e.g., Q proves n+m = n+m and uniqueness ∀y ((n+m)=y → y = n+m)); representability of these primitives serves as base case for closure arguments.
